sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
Markets enter the new week quiet on the surface but with a live policy question underneath: the priced odds of a September 16 Fed hike sit at 57.9% (frame policy path, as-of 2026-09-07), so the front end is doing the work. This week's own bar feed was down (apex bars returned 502 across sectors and themes), so sector-rotation and theme-performance readings are unavailable — treat leadership claims as unsupported this week.

What is priced and dated: 10-year yield 4.79%, up ~1bp from a prior 4.784%; 2-year 4.375%, essentially flat; the 2s10s curve at 41.5bp. High-yield spreads at 2.65% (as-of 2026-09-03), a touch tighter — credit is not flagging stress. VIX at 14.52, up +0.21pts, still a low-teens regime. SPY's dealer gamma flip sits at 768.35 versus spot near 770 (equity internals, as-of 2026-09-08), so positioning is close to the pivot rather than deep in stabilizing territory.

Headlines corroborate the macro frame, not more: Unusual Whales at 2026-09-08T00:03:48Z notes gold holding near $4,400 with markets pricing '~60% odds of a Fed hike next week,' consistent with the frame's 57.9%. Commodities show gold 4418.92 (-0.25%) and WTI crude 92.51 (+1.13%) — a firmer oil tape is the inflation cross-current the same headline flags. Japan Q2 revised GDP came in +1.4% annualized (2026-09-07T23:51:01Z), below the ~1.8% estimate, and average cash earnings +4.7% beat 3.8% (2026-09-07T23:30:49Z) — reflationary abroad.

Judgement: with a hike near a coin-flip and gamma near the flip level, the setup favors range-respect until the front end resolves. That reading rests on the 57.9% policy print and the 768.35 flip being accurate as-of their stamps; both predate today's session.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
The week is organized around one dated fork: the September 16 FOMC, priced at HIKE 57.9% (frame calendar). At a near coin-flip, the market has no consensus to lean on, and the front end (2yr 4.375%) will re-rate hard on the outcome. Watch for confirmation in the same instruments: a decisive break of the 2s10s from 41.5bp, a move in the hike probability away from the high-50s, and HY spreads leaving the 2.65% zone. If spreads widen while equities hold, that is the tell the tape is under-pricing tightening; if they stay pinned, the range holds.

The US CPI print flagged in the 2026-09-08T00:03:48Z headline as capping gold's upside is the near-term input into that hike question — a hot CPI pushes the 57.9% higher and pressures the long end past 4.79%; a soft one relieves it. Crude firming (WTI 92.51, +1.13%) is the reverse risk to any disinflation story: sustained oil strength feeds headline inflation and keeps the hawkish path alive.

Dealer positioning is the second axis. With the SPY gamma flip at 768.35 and spot near 770, the market sits just above the pivot; a slip below it removes the stabilizing bid and lets realized volatility rise from a VIX base of 14.52. The observable is simple — hold above 768.35 and dips get bought; break and hold below and the same level caps rallies.

Single-name catalyst: ADBE reports post-market 2026-09-10 (earnings confirmed, daysToEarnings 2), implied move 6.93%, IV rank 68.84 — the one dated event inside the week for our universe, and a read on software demand ahead of the Fed.

Limitation to carry forward: sector and theme rotation is uninformed this week because the bar feed was down (502 across XLB–XLY, DBA/MOS/NTR/DE). Any leadership conclusion should wait for bars to return; do not infer rotation from price memory. Reverse risk to the range view: a clean CPI-plus-Fed resolution can trend, not chop — the flip level and spread behavior tell you which.
